text:
maya: Heads up — since the networkpolicy rollout last night we're seeing RDMA handshakes fail between pods across AZs (us-west-2a -> us-west-2b). GPU jobs start, then OOM/retries once kv-syncs time out. :grimacing:

alex: Can you paste the failing logs or a quick iperf? Is this only RDMA or plain TCP too?

maya: TCP also degraded. iperf from pod-a (us-west-2a) -> pod-b (us-west-2b):
```
iperf3 -c 10.1.23.45 -t 10
[SUM]   0.00-10.00  sec  254 KBytes   208 Kbits/sec  8292             sender
```
lots of retransmits.

ryan: Was there a calico/netpol controller change in the rollout? infra-bot, any deploys around 02:11 UTC?

infra-bot: deploy:netpol-controller v2.6.1 promoted to prod at 2026-03-16T02:07:12Z by @ops-ci (rollout: 60% -> 100%).

maya: yeah that matches. I also grabbed the NetworkPolicy that was applied to gpu namespaces:
```
kubectl -n gpu-prod get networkpolicy gpu-egress -o yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: gpu-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.0.0/16
        except: [10.1.128.0/17]
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: kv-sync
```
Note: our VPC range is 10.0.0.0/16 across AZs, not 10.1.0.0/16. (PR typo)

alex: that CIDR typo would block cross-AZ pod traffic — but why did it manifest as iptables chain duplication?

maya: when I inspected node iptables, I found duplicate chains with similar names and different rules; looks like controller created overlapping chains and kube-proxy's chain ordering caused the wrong one to be hit. snippet: 
```
# iptables -S | grep CLAW_NETPOL
-N CLAW_NETPOL-0
-N CLAW_NETPOL-1
-A CLAW_NETPOL-0 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -j RETURN
-A CLAW_NETPOL-1 -s 10.1.0.0/16 -j RETURN
-A KUBE-SERVICES -j CLAW_NETPOL-1
```
so traffic matched the chain with the wrong CIDR. chain indexes were non-deterministic after the controller restart.

ryan: oh — controller v2.6.1 had a bug where it creates per-namespace chains and appends duplicates when label reconciliation races. Ticket was opened in staging but didn't fail fast.

ken: +1 saw conntrack counts spike on nodes (conntrack entries > 1.2M), probably due to packets being DROPped and retries stacking.

maya: actions taken so far:
- rolled back netpol-controller to v2.6.0 on a couple of nodes (patch rollback)
- corrected NetworkPolicy CIDR in gpu-prod to 10.0.0.0/16
- restarted calico-node on affected nodes to flush iptables chains and force proper reconciliation

alex: after the restart, can you re-run iperf and check RDMA handshake logs?

maya: re-run after restart:
```
iperf3 -c 10.1.23.45 -t 10
[SUM]   0.00-10.00  sec  9.1 GBytes  7.85 Gbits/sec                  receiver
```
RDMA handshakes successful again, kv-sync errors gone.

ryan: good. Root cause summary: 1) bad CIDR in NetworkPolicy (human typo) + 2) netpol-controller bug that created duplicate/ordering-sensitive iptables chains during a reconciliation race. Combined caused egress to match the wrong chain and drop east-west traffic.

ken: follow-ups: add an e2e that validates cluster-wide CIDR in netpol manifests before apply, and add controller dedupe for chains. Also add an alert on conntrack > 800k and iptables duplicate chain count > 1.

maya: created a quick runbook in ops-runbooks: steps to rollback controller, fix NP, restart calico-node, and verify with iperf + rdma logs. Will open PR for controller fix and an alert rule.

alex: GH issue?

maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/netpol-controller/issues/412 — added repro, logs, and suggested fix.

ryan: nice. Can we also add a policy lint in CI to catch common mistakes (CIDR mismatch w/cluster-cidr)?

maya: on it. I'll add a CI check and a follow-up ticket for the dedupe patch.

ken: thanks all. marking this thread resolved for now — will monitor alerts for the next 24h. :thumbsup:
